en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is an active stratovolcano famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape.
The Philippine eagle, one of the largest and rarest eagles in the world, lives in the forests of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake located inside a volcanic crater on Volcano Island.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing 2,954 meters above sea level.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea protects hundreds of coral and fish species.
The native abaca plant produces strong fibers used to make traditional Manila rope and paper.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is an underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Philippines experiences a wet southwest monsoon called habagat and a dry northeast monsoon called amihan.
Bohol province features the Chocolate Hills, which are over 1,200 symmetrical limestone mounds.
The tamaraw is a critically endangered dwarf buffalo found only on the island of Mindoro.
The Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into the Cordillera mountains over 2,000 years ago.
